D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Wix documents the general hosted MCP alongside separate Wix Site MCP and Wix WebMCP products. Within the general server, documentation separates account-level management from site-scoped API tools and directs agents through a WixREADME entry point.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official Wix SDK documentation has a named tool list at https://dev.wix.com/docs/sdk/articles/use-the-wix-mcp/about-the-wix-mcp; this inventory contains 18 names, all stated as enabled by default. The official repository README lists 12 earlier tools. Claude's third-party connector listing displays 11 names, while Glama reports 25 observed tools and Agent Discoverability exposes a 29-tool list. Those catalogues differ from the official docs and include additional or differently surfaced tools; the endpoint itself could not be authenticated for tools/list. No catalogue-only tools were added because the available catalogue evidence did not establish their exact membership in this endpoint.

List sites associated with the Wix account.
Fetch a site ID, properties and installed apps by name.
Perform one REST API call for an account and selected site.

Prompt the user for feedback and send it to Wix.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server's tool definitions and initialize instructions were not available. The public repository contains configuration and documentation, not the running server implementation or serialized MCP definitions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The reviewed docs do not provide a definitive human-versus-MCP exclusion list. The MCP can execute site APIs and account-level site actions; API operations or product controls not exposed by the published tool list may remain available through Wix interfaces or APIs. Wix's REST and product documentation describe a much broader platform than this MCP tool list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Wix documents that WixREADME routes tasks and is called first for most management tasks. The Agent Discoverability catalogue reproduces stronger wording, including “MANDATORY FIRST STEP” and instructions to use particular tool sequences. These are agent-facing instructions; no public handler code confirms server-side enforcement.
F_documentation.governance_promises: No MCP-specific privacy, retention, AI-training or audit promise found in reviewed Wix MCP pages. OAuth metadata identifies offline_access as the only supported scope.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Wix describes the MCP as enabling documentation search, code writing and API calls on Wix sites. Its documentation says all listed tools are enabled by default.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: No server implementation was available to compare against the documented behavior. Tool defaults and workflow language are documentation claims; the endpoint's OAuth protection is independently evidenced by the 401 response and metadata.

contradictions: The official README's earlier tool table lists 12 tools, while Wix's SDK documentation updated 19 August 2026 names 18 tools. The latter includes WixREADME, BrowseWixRESTDocsMenu, SearchWixAPISpec, GetSiteContext and ExecuteWixAPI, among other additions.
Claude's connector directory lists 11 tools; this is fewer than the official 18-tool list and omits several documented tools.

Glama reports 25 observed tools and Agent Discoverability displays 29 tools, exceeding the official list. These counts may reflect newer or connector-specific tools; the authenticated endpoint could not be inspected to resolve the difference.

The Wix documentation describes both HTTP and SSE connection types, while third-party listings characterize the endpoint as Streamable HTTP or report the SSE URL. The input endpoint itself returned 401 before transport negotiation.
observations_for_research: The official tool descriptions establish differentiated paths: recipes and documentation lookup, site-scoped single or chained API execution, account-level site management, image upload, and feedback submission.
WixREADME is documented as a routing entry point, so its instructions can affect which tools the agent selects before any API call.
Feedback is exposed as an action that prompts the user and sends the resulting feedback to Wix.

OAuth metadata advertises offline_access only, while Wix's setup docs also mention API-key configuration for some clients; the exact endpoint authorization flow is established through the provided metadata.
